jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Arts Management (music Industry)
jobs.description: Assistant Professor of Arts Management (music Industry) Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details POSTING INFORMATION Internal Title Assistant Professor of Arts Management (music Industry) Position Type Tenure-track School/Area School of the Arts Department Arts Management Position Description The Arts Management Program in the School of the Arts at the College of Charleston (charleston.edu/arts-management) invites applications for the Assistant Professor of Arts Management position. This is a tenure-track position, and the anticipated start date is August 16, 2026. Responsibilities at this rank include teaching a minimum of six courses per year. While the teaching load covers the broader Arts Management curriculum, this position serves as the primary faculty lead for the music industry concentration including oversight of the student-run record label. The incumbent will also engage with arts and cultural organizations, contribute to program development, mentor and advise undergraduate students, and perform service to the College, community, and profession as appropriate. Moreover, the successful candidate is expected to maintain an active research agenda or program of creative scholarship, including peer-reviewed publications, industry-focused research, or significant professional creative contributions, commensurate with expectations for tenure and promotion. Preference for this position will be given to candidates with professional experience in the music industry and connections therein, demonstrated college student oversight responsibilities inclusive of experiential learning, as well as expertise in one or more of the following areas: strategic planning, arts policy, fundraising and grant writing, creativity, arts presenting, and arts marketing. Candidates must possess a demonstrated ability to teach college-level courses as well as conduct quality research in one or more of the above-stated areas, with a preference for the music industry. Minimum Credentials: A terminal degree in arts management or a closely related field is required. If the degree is in a related field, at least 18 hours of arts management-related graduate coursework is required. The successful candidate for the rank of assistant professor will have 3-5+ years of experience in the music business/industry, arts management, or a closely related field which can include a combination of teaching arts management and/or music industry courses on a college level and management experience in the professional field. Candidates with both undergraduate and graduate teaching experience as well as online teaching are preferred. Candidates without online teaching experience will be asked to complete an online education readiness course at the College of Charleston. College of Charleston: The College of Charleston / University of Charleston is a nationally recognized public liberal arts and sciences university located in the heart of historic Charleston, SC. Since our founding in 1770, we have maintained a strong liberal arts curriculum. The university encompasses the unusual combination of an exceptional faculty, historic campus, coastal location, modern facilities and cutting-edge programs. The student body numbers approximately 10,400 in undergraduate and graduate programs combined. If you have questions or require accommodations during the online application process, please contact the Office of Human Resources at jobs@cofc.edu. For more information, please visit https://charleston.edu/equal-opportunity-programs How to Apply Online: Applicants should apply online at jobs.cofc.edu and will be asked to include: Letter of application: including the candidate’s ability to advance the mission of the Arts Management Program as well as the music industry concentration, and current and projected research agenda; Curriculum vitae; Teaching philosophy. Evidence of quality teaching and sample syllabi are encouraged; One representative publication; Unofficial graduate transcripts (official transcripts will be required for hiring); Contact information for three references. Please direct questions regarding the position to Dr. Hsin-Ching Wu, Assistant Professor and Chair of the Search Committee at wuh@cofc.edu. Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications. The review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Posting Details POSTING INFORMATION Internal Title Chair of the Engineering Department Position Type Tenure-track School/Area School of Engineering, Computer Science, and Mathematics Department Engineering Position Description The School of Engineering, Computing, and Mathematics (SECM) at the College of Charleston invites applications for a tenured position as Chair of the Department of Engineering at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor, with an anticipated start date of January 2026. Appointment rank and tenure status will be based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will provide visionary leadership to guide the department’s continued growth in academic programs, student enrollment, and national reputation. Candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education, high-quality teaching, and maintaining an active, productive research agenda. Established in 2023, the Department of Engineering currently offers Bachelor of Science degrees in Electrical Engineering and Systems Engineering. A new interdisciplinary Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Integrated Engineering and Business is in development, and a Biomedical Engineering program is currently in the early planning stages. This position presents a unique opportunity for an innovative leader to shape a young and evolving department during an exciting period of strategic expansion. SECM offers a friendly, dynamic, and collaborative environment, with ample opportunities for interdisciplinary partnerships across the university’s ten schools, including the Schools of Business, Education, Natural & Environmental Sciences, and the newly formed School of Health Sciences. The university is located just blocks from the Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC), providing opportunities for collaboration in medical and health-related education and research. Additionally, South Carolina is home to a growing industrial base, including leading manufacturers and a vibrant medical device and healthcare industry. Priority will be given to candidates with expertise in systems engineering, mechanical engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or a related field. jobs.title: Dean of Students
jobs.description: Dean of Students Employment Application Department Student Life Status Full-Time Time Period 40 hours/12 months Available June 1, 2026 Description The Dean of Students provides mission-driven, strategic leadership at Columbia International University, advancing a holistic approach that strengthens spiritual formation, discipleship, and student success. This role leads a comprehensive portfolio of student life functions, including spiritual formation, residential life, student engagement, health and wellness, and student conduct, ensuring advancement of CIU’s mission of preparing students to impact the nations with the message of Christ. As a key partner across campus, the Dean of Students champions a cohesive student experience from enrollment through graduation, with a particular emphasis on belonging, discipleship, and persistence within a mission-fit community. Responsibilities Cultivate the spiritual formation of the student body by: Providing vision and leadership for campus-wide spiritual formation initiatives. Advancing a culture of discipleship that integrates spiritual growth into all aspects of the student experience. Developing and implementing intentional discipleship pathways and leadership development opportunities for students. Encouraging evangelical unity and fostering a campus environment marked by biblical community and shared mission. Engage directly with students through mentoring, discipleship, and teaching in classroom and chapel settings as appropriate. Promoting character development and spiritual maturity in alignment with CIU’s mission and community standards. Create a vibrant campus community aligned with biblical values by: Championing a student experience that reflects CIU’s commitment to mission fit, aligning student expectations, institutional values, and community life. Ensuring a safe, supportive, and Christ-centered campus environment conducive to learning, belonging, and personal growth. Overseeing student conduct processes that reflect a restorative approach, using sound judgment and discernment in addressing behavioral concerns. Overseeing health services and mental health support, ensuring students are cared for holistically. Strengthening residential life to foster environments that support academic success, community engagement, and biblical discipleship. Promoting meaningful student engagement through programs and initiatives that build community and connection. Identifying and addressing barriers to student success across social, spiritual, and personal dimensions in collaboration with campus partners. Provide strategic leadership for the Student Life department by: Leading the ongoing development and refinement of a cohesive student life model that supports institutional growth and student success. Partnering across campus to strengthen student persistence and retention through data-informed, student-centered strategies. Building systems, processes, and team structures that ensure the sustainability and scalability of student life programs. Providing leadership and direction to Student Life staff, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Overseeing the Student Life budget, ensuring responsible stewardship and alignment with institutional priorities. Ensuring compliance with Title IX, legal, and accreditation requirements. Leading systematic assessment and planning efforts to evaluate and improve student life programs and outcomes. Regularly reviewing and developing Student Life policies to ensure alignment with institutional mission, legal standards, and best practices. Qualifications Demonstrated commitment to CIU’s biblical, doctrinal, and community life standards, as well as its mission and educational philosophy. Proven leadership of a comprehensive student life program within higher education. Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence across organizational lines and collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, and senior leadership. Strategic thinker with the ability to translate vision into clear priorities, plans, and measurable outcomes. Experience leading teams through growth, change, or organizational development. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills with diverse constituencies, including students, families, faculty, and administrators. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, staff, and budgets effectively. Strong problem-solving and conflict resolution skills. Experience providing student care, counseling, and discipleship from a biblical perspective. Knowledge of and experience with Title IX compliance and student conduct processes. Demonstrated effectiveness in public speaking, teaching, and group facilitation. Minimum of five years of progressive leadership experience in student development or a related field Master’s degree in a relevant field required; additional post-secondary training or advanced degree in student development or higher education preferred. Benefits CIU provides a benefits package that includes: Health Plan; 401(k) plan with match opportunity; Employer provided group life insurance; Long term disability insurance; Vacation days, holidays, sick leave, family leave; Educational benefits: tuition reduction for PreK3-Graduate. The ideal candidate will also be interested and credentialed to teach interdisciplinary courses that expand our current offerings in the liberal arts. jobs.description: Visiting Instructor of Public Health (2 positions) Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details POSTING INFORMATION Internal Title Visiting Instructor of Public Health (2 positions) Position Type Instructor School/Area School of Health Sciences Department Department of Public Health Sciences and Administration Position Description The College of Charleston invites qualified applicants for two full-time visiting instructor positions within the Department of Public Health Sciences and Administration beginning in August 2026. The successful candidate will join an active department that offers undergraduate degrees in public health (both B.S. and B.A.) and health services administration and management (B.S.) within the expanding School of Health Sciences. We currently have 10 full-time teacher-scholars that serve approximately 400 undergraduate majors. We are committed to preparing and equipping the next generation of health professionals and are seeking applicants who share our mission and want to engage with undergraduate students in and outside the classroom through dynamic teaching, professional advising, and mentorship. Located in the heart of historic Charleston, South Carolina, the College of Charleston is a nationally recognized public university. Founded in 1770, the College is the oldest educational institution south of Virginia and the 13th oldest in the US. The College of Charleston is among the nation’s top universities for quality education, student life, and affordability. Its beautiful and historic campus, combined with contemporary facilities, cutting-edge programs, and accessible faculty, attracts students from across the US and around the world. Over 10,000 undergraduates and approximately 500 graduate students at the College enjoy a small campus feel blended with the advantages and diversity of a mid-sized, urban university. Students work closely with a committed faculty that is made up of more than 500 distinguished teacher-scholars. And the city of Charleston – world-renowned for its history, architecture, culture, and coastal environment – serves as a living and learning laboratory for experiences in business, science, technology, teaching, the humanities, languages, and the arts. The responsibilities of a visiting instructor include 1) providing high-quality instruction in four course sections per semester within the public health program, 2) offering professional (non-academic) mentoring for majors, 3) actively participating in the development and advancement of curriculum and accreditation, 4) working collaboratively within the program and department to help meet stated goals and objectives, and 5) committing to a liberal arts and sciences undergraduate education. At minimum, applicants must possess a master’s degree in public health or a closely related discipline from an accredited institution prior to the August 16, 2026 start date. Applicants must demonstrate the ability to teach undergraduate students effectively and a strong commitment to teaching excellence. We seek individuals whose teaching and/or professional experiences support instruction across a broad range of courses within the public health curriculum; areas of expertise are open. Candidates with diverse and relevant educational and professional experiences are encouraged to apply. Interested individuals should apply online at https://jobs.cofc.edu, and include 1) a curriculum vitae, 2) cover letter that describes your teaching philosophy including courses capable and interested in instructing, 3) unofficial graduate transcripts, and 4) contact information for three references.
